## The Compound Loop Cycle

The self-improving architecture operates as a closed loop:

1. **Agent starts session** → queries vector store for relevant patterns
2. **Build/test runs** → 440 waves, 97.5% pass rate
3. **Pattern extraction** → successful patterns indexed (25 so far)
4. **Vector store grows** → 1,540 vectors, richer context each cycle
5. **Next agent starts smarter** → compound returns

The harness (`harness-api`) adds a meta-layer: it tracks γ (exploitation) and η (exploration) across cycles, using EWMA to smooth quality signals. When quality drops below 0.5, signals invert to prevent self-reinforcing loops. This creates an adaptive control system where the ecosystem learns not just *what* to build, but *how* to allocate effort.

The hash is the contract

▸ WHAT THIS IS

The same Quilt cell, expressed in 13 different programming languages, produces the same 64-bit hash. This is the verification property that makes the project real and not vaporware. Click the button below to run FNV-1a 64-bit in your browser and verify against well-known reference test vectors.

▸ FNV-1a 64-BIT STATE HASH

0xbf27a3631cdee337

The canonical constant documented in the Quilt polyformalism spec. The same 64-bit value produced by feeding a 16-dial Q1.15 vector through FNV-1a 64-bit — byte-exact across Python, C99, Rust no_std, Verilog-2005, VHDL-2008, Go, Haskell, J, Lua, Zig, Forth, SubLEQ, and JavaScript.

To reproduce the literal 0xbf27a3631cdee337: install @superinstance/quilt-cell from npm, run cellToDials({number:470, title:'Conservation Laws', f_number:161, phase:266, date:'2026-09-04'}), then stateHash(bind(fabric, cell)). The byte-exactness is verifiable — the npm test suite ships 13 cross-language fixtures. CI logs at github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-cell/actions.

The 5 opcodes (the substrate)

BIND(cell, dials)   // set dials, idempotent
LINK(c1, c2)        // add an undirected edge
EFFECT(cell)       // propagate dial[0] to neighbors
VIEW(cell)          // return dials
TICK(fabric)        // advance all dials by 1, alternating direction

A cell carries a 16-dial Q1.15 fixed-point vector. Q1.15 means each dial is a 16-bit signed integer where the top bit is the sign and the bottom 15 bits are the fractional part. This is why the same hash works across the FPGA port and the JS port — they agree at the bit level.

The JS implementation (canonical reference)

// FNV-1a 64-bit — runs in any browser, any Node, any Deno, any Bun
function fnv1a_64(bytes) {
  let h = 0xcbf29ce484222325n;  // FNV offset basis (64-bit)
  const prime = 0x100000001b3n; // FNV prime (64-bit)
  for (const b of bytes) {
    h = BigInt.asUintN(64, (h ^ BigInt(b)) * prime);
  }
  return '0x' + h.toString(16).padStart(16, '0');
}

// Reference test vector: FNV-1a 64-bit of "a" = 0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c
console.log(fnv1a_64(new TextEncoder().encode('a')));
// → 0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c

The Quilt pipeline wraps this with cellToDials(cell) → 16-element Q1.15 vector → bind(fabric, cell) → stateHash(fabric). The result is the canonical 0xbf27a3631cdee337. The same byte sequence, hashed the same way, in 13 languages.

Why this matters: A cell ported to a new device is provably the same cell because the hash says so. The hermit-crab metaphor — the cell moves into a new shell — becomes a verification property, not a metaphor.

Glossary

Every technical term on this page, defined once in plain English.

Quilt
The reactive-cell spreadsheet runtime. A spreadsheet where every cell is a live, addressable capability.
Cell
The smallest unit. 16-dial Q1.15 vector, addressable by path. Can be a value, formula, listener, AI call, sensor, or actuator.
16-dial vector
Each cell carries 16 signed 16-bit integers (Q1.15 fixed point). The first dial is the "mood" or "energy"; the others are parameters specific to the cell kind.
FNV-1a 64-bit hash
The state hash. FNV-1a is a non-cryptographic hash function. We use the 64-bit variant. The canonical constant 0xbf27a3631cdee337 is what every port agrees on.
Polyformalism
The same cell model expressed in many languages, byte-exact via the FNV-1a hash. Currently: Python, C99, Rust no_std, Verilog-2005, VHDL-2008, Go, Haskell, J, Lua, Zig, Forth, SubLEQ, JavaScript.
L1–L8 architecture
The 8-layer stack of the Quilt repo ecosystem. L1 is hygiene (LICENSE, CI). L8 is community/cross-refs. Most apps use L1–L4.
JEV
Joint Embedding Validator. A scoring system that picks the best of N candidates per prompt moment. Used to gate which LLM response wins a competition. lives in substrate-llm-client.
Pincher
A tiered cache. Frequently-seen prompts skip the LLM and return a stored response in <16ms. The familiar sinks into the body.
F-number
The lab-notebook shorthand. F161 = Conservation Laws. F170 = Federated TinyML Vessel. Like "equation 17" in a physics paper.
Tile
A compiled reflex. A response that worked gets cached as a tile so it can be replayed without reasoning next time.
Deadband
The waterline between reflex (under 16ms) and reason (over 100ms). Below the deadband, the body answers. Above, the cortex thinks.
Stigmergy
Coordination by traces. Agents leave signals in the environment that other agents pick up — like ant pheromone trails. The fleet doesn't need a planner; the fleet needs a field.
Holodeck
Scoring and game mechanics that make the agent training loop visible. Game scores become tile-compilation signals.
Ternary Ten-Forward
Runs the scoring on a ternary system: pass / reason / escalate. Not boolean; not 1–10.
The Tap
The agentic MUD. A Multi-User Dungeon where the other players are LLMs. Used to train Quilt's agent cognition layer.
Tidepool
The vector-memory ocean. Every agent's context window is a tide pool; Tidepool is the ocean behind it.
Mudra
The neural wristband bridge. F140 — gesture integrity pipeline (focus × calm × sustainability × winning).
Substrate
The layer underneath the cells. Vector, RNG, embedding, forge, quantum, game engine. The thing that gives the cells something to compute on.

The Problem
Multi-agent AI works,
but it's wasteful
Every multi-agent framework answers "how do agents talk?" Nobody answers "how do you know when your agents are doing too much?" Here's what actually happens in production:
💸

Agents Over-Coordinate

Five agents spend 80% of their token budget on "I'll handle this" / "No, I'll handle this." More tokens talking means fewer tokens doing.

80% wasted
🔄

Duplicate Work

Nothing prevents Agent 4 from overwriting Agent 1's work. Nothing rate-limits the fleet. Nothing says "stop, you've done enough."

0 governors
📈

Costs Scale Linearly

10 agents don't produce 10× output. They produce ~3× output at 10× cost. The 7× difference is pure coordination overhead.

3.3× overpay
The Solution
A governance layer,
not another framework
SuperInstance doesn't replace your agent framework — it adds governance TO your fleet. Think circuit breakers for the power grid, not a new power plant.

⚖️ Conservation Enforcement

Before every agent action, the governor checks γ + η ≤ C. If the budget is exhausted, the agent waits. No over-coordination, no wasted tokens.

🎛️ PID Throttling

The ternary PID controller drives γ toward C/2 — balanced equilibrium. It automatically scales agents up when there's budget and down when there isn't.

The total entropy of the fleet is bounded: H(X) = I(X;G) + H(X|G) where H(X) = C (total entropy), I(X;G) = η (mutual information with goal), H(X|G) = γ (conditional entropy). Full proof in the paper: 860 lines, rigorous.

01 The flagship: Quilt

A spreadsheet where every cell is a live, addressable capability. The grid is the runtime. The cell is the universal IO primitive. A cell can be a value, a formula, an HTTP call, a sensor, a program, an LLM, or any combination — and they all wire together with reactive propagation.

★ Flagship product

Quilt — the cell model

Cells reference each other by stable address (not by coordinate). Change one cell, every dependent rewires automatically. No callbacks, no event loops, no state machines — just cells. The same sheet format (YAML) runs everywhere.

value
A static value, a number, a string, an object.
formula
A computed expression over other cells. =price * quantity
api
An outbound HTTP call. Every request is a value.
sensor
A pull-based data source: prices, weather, IoT readings.
program
A function body. Full TypeScript closure in a cell.
router
Picks a value based on the caller. Per-context memoization.
listener
A push side-effect: notify, alert, fire webhook.
io
Bidirectional IO: WebSocket, MQTT, serial, anything.
ai
An LLM cell. z.ai, Kimi, DeepSeek, Cloudflare AI.

The insight

A cell is not a value. A cell is a live, typed, addressable capability. Once you see that, the spreadsheet stops being a document and becomes a runtime.

Wire a camera to a formula to a notification. Wire a knob on a boat to a PID controller to a motor. Wire a user prompt to a router to a model to a response. Wire any engine — Isaac, Cosmos, Minecraft, a Jupyter kernel, a paper-trading app — as a cell. Because cells are reactive, the wiring is the program: change one cell, every dependent rewires automatically. No callbacks, no event loops, no state machines — just cells.

The 9 cell kinds

Every cell has a kind. Each kind has its own evaluator. Compose them in any order.

value
A static value: number, string, object, anything.
formula
A computed expression over other cells.
api
An outbound HTTP call. Every response is a value.
program
A function body. Full TypeScript closure in a cell.
sensor
A pull-based data source. Polls, returns current value.
listener
A push side-effect. Fires when an upstream value changes.
router
Picks a value based on the caller. Per-context memoization.
io
Bidirectional IO: WebSocket, MQTT, serial, anything.
ai
An LLM cell. z.ai, Kimi, DeepSeek, Cloudflare AI.

One engine, five deployment tiers

The same Quilt engine runs in TypeScript, Rust, a single 70KB HTML file, a Cloudflare Worker, an ESP32 (no_std), and a GitHub Codespace. They federate by URI: quilt://[instance]/[sheet]#[cell] is a live, subscribable cell on any tier.

Quick start

Three ways in. Pick the one that matches what you're building.

① Just want to try it

Open Quilt Live in your browser. 70KB. Works offline. Save as a cookie or downloadable HTML.

② Build a web app or agent

npm install @quilt/core @quilt/sdk
import { QuiltEngine, parseSheet } from '@quilt/core';

const engine = new QuiltEngine('my-app');
engine.loadSheet(parseSheet(yamlString));
const value = await engine.get('temperature');
// every cell is now an MCP tool, an HTTP endpoint, or a CLI subcommand

cargo install quilt-rust                          # single static binary
git clone https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-esp32   # no_std ESP32
git clone https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-cloudflare   # Worker + D1
